subject.title: Session model pinning persists indefinitely: snap-back probe (PR #82676) defeated by origin-field pollution upstream — repros on 2026.5.28 through 2026.6.7-beta.1, byte-identical paths

question: Should automatic fallback remain a persisted, probe-backed session route with corrected provenance and Doctor repair, or should OpenClaw instead adopt the broader behavior of clearing automatic fallback state after every successful fallback?
rationale: Both paths can prevent indefinite pinning, but they differ in the persisted-session contract established by the merged primary-probe behavior and in upgrade semantics for existing sessions.

options.title: Repair provenance and migrate polluted auto state
options.body: Keep the current probe-backed automatic fallback model, write the configured primary as origin, and repair only proven stale automatic entries through Doctor.

options.title: Make successful automatic fallback turn-scoped
options.body: Adopt the broader clear-after-success behavior, which changes the current session persistence contract and needs explicit compatibility approval.

options.title: Pause for a narrower root-cause split
options.body: First separate wrong-candidate selection after hot reload from provenance pollution if they prove to be independent defects.

recommendation.title: Repair provenance and migrate polluted auto state
recommendation.body: Keep the current probe-backed automatic fallback model, write the configured primary as origin, and repair only proven stale automatic entries through Doctor.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice directly concerns the probe-backed fallback behavior introduced by the merged fallback-recovery implementation.
